concept.title: Task topics
concept.abstract: This chapter explains DITA task topics as the primary structure for documenting goal-oriented procedures through prerequisites, context, sequential actions, verification points, results, and follow-up activities. It covers the complete task information model, including steps, substeps, choices, choice tables, images, tables, and procedural metadata, while demonstrating best practices for creating clear, actionable, and user-centered instructions. Through practical scenarios, the chapter illustrates how to model real-world workflows such as installation, configuration, deployment, administration, and operational procedures using semantically correct DITA task elements.

conbody.p: Task topics provide step-by-step instructions that guide users to complete a specific goal. Every step must be an action a user performs.
